# Reselling per-use services at a profit: what to sell, at what price, and in what order: 18 October 2026

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/per-use-resale.mjs` from docs/per-use-resale-data-2026-10-18.json and tests/per-use-resale-table.ts. Do not edit by hand: tests/per-use-resale.test.ts fails when this file is stale. -->

**An analysis for the owner, not a change.** No price, limit or gate in code changes, and sales stay closed. Every rate is the lowest that keeps 60% per customer at full use under the repository's own margin code (lib/receiving-costs.ts `unitUnder`, sizing reading), sold the only way the owner allows: **prepaid credits, bought before use, use stopping automatically at zero** (docs/pack-cost-decomposition-2026-10-18.md, option 3). Post-paid billing (overage or a line on the renewal invoice) is not offered: the customer pays first, then receives.

**The more a creator uses, the more Marktmorgen earns** on every service marked sell: each credit keeps 60% however it is spent, so profit grows with use and never turns into a loss. What it cannot do is be cheap: under the 60% rule and the receiving model a unit sells at about twenty times its cost (docs/pack-cost-decomposition-2026-10-18.md), so for messaging and calls, where HighLevel passes supplier rates through, Marktmorgen would be many times dearer. A position above competitors there is not reachable by price; for email, video and AI it comes from the plan's included figures, with credits only for the overflow.

## Compliance and engineering, per service

| Service | Legal and compliance burden (to review with counsel; not legal advice) | Engineering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extra list emails (as today: Resend's rate) | CAN-SPAM, GDPR and ePrivacy consent: already carried by lib/email.ts, the list's consent and unsubscribe, lib/mail-health.ts | Small: the meters exist (lib/email.ts EmailMeter); a balance drawn on after the plan's figure, the purchase and its page |
| Extra list emails, sent by Amazon SES only (if built) | As above; SES reviews an account at 5% bounced or 0.1% complaints (lib/ses.ts) | Medium: credits' emails sent with sendBatch's `only: "amazon"` and held, never handed to Resend, while Amazon is down; the page says they can wait |
| Video hours watched | None new | Small: lib/video-admission-rules.ts already counts and refuses hours; the balance after the plan's figure |
| AI writing jobs (with five answers each) | None new (lib/ai-spend.ts already holds every call to its ceiling) | Small: the AI ceiling's company total (`companyMicroUsd`) must count what credits buy |
| AI captions (a minute of video, one language) | None new; captions help accessibility | Already sold as its own charge, paid before the work (lib/auto-captions-rules.ts); moving it into credits is small |
| SMS (US, 10DLC long code) | TCPA (prior express written consent for marketing texts, its record kept), A2P 10DLC brand and campaign registration per creator, STOP/HELP handled at once, quiet hours under several state laws, CTIA guidelines; EU ePrivacy prior consent | Large: a supplier integration, number provisioning and 10DLC registration per creator, inbound webhooks, consent records, STOP, quiet hours by recipient time zone |
| WhatsApp marketing message (US) | WhatsApp Business policy opt-in, approved templates outside the 24-hour window, Meta business verification, commerce policy; TCPA-style consent where applicable; EU ePrivacy | Large: a WhatsApp Business Account per creator through a provider, template approval flow, the 24-hour window, inbound handling |
| Phone calls, recorded (US, outbound) | TCPA for autodialed or prerecorded calls, two-party consent to record in several states, caller ID (STIR/SHAKEN), do-not-call lists | Large: numbers, a calling client, recording consent prompts, storage and deletion of recordings |
| AI voice agent on a call | As calls, and the FCC's February 2024 declaratory ruling that AI-generated voices are "artificial" under the TCPA (prior express consent); disclosure that the caller is an AI | Very large: everything calls need, an agent, its language model held to a ceiling |

## The order to build

1. **Extra list emails (as today: Resend's rate)**: Small: the meters exist (lib/email.ts EmailMeter); a balance drawn on after the plan's figure, the purchase and its page.
2. **Extra list emails, sent by Amazon SES only (if built)**: Medium: credits' emails sent with sendBatch's `only: "amazon"` and held, never handed to Resend, while Amazon is down; the page says they can wait.
3. **Video hours watched**: Small: lib/video-admission-rules.ts already counts and refuses hours; the balance after the plan's figure.
4. **AI writing jobs (with five answers each)**: Small: the AI ceiling's company total (`companyMicroUsd`) must count what credits buy.
5. **AI captions (a minute of video, one language)**: Already sold as its own charge, paid before the work (lib/auto-captions-rules.ts); moving it into credits is small.

Not before something structural changes: SMS, WhatsApp, calls and AI voice. Each would sell at about twenty times the supplier's rate against competitors that pass it through, carries a fixed cost per creator each month before the first use, and brings the heaviest consent rules; AI voice has a cost no page bounds. "Paid third-party services" in general are not evaluated: no specific service was named, and each would need its own reading.

## What is not known

- **Demand** for any of these, at any price. No sale has been open.
- **Meta's own WhatsApp rate card** (its page links a file that was not read) and **Vonage's US rates** (not stated on its page); Plivo's listed price stands in for WhatsApp, and Vonage is not used.
- **Twilio's volume tiers**: its page lists standard rates only; the standard rate is the dearest and is the one used.
- **Stripe's own pricing page** was not re-read (docs/pack-cost-decomposition-2026-10-18.md); the receiving model keeps the dearer of Stripe and Paddle.
- **The legal analysis** is a list of burdens to review, not advice and not a finding that any service is lawful as built.
